intro: Picture taking the lift up to the top floor in the evening and finding an infinity pool whose edge seems to spill into the horizon, looking down over Si Racha Bay with cargo ships anchored in the distance, while the other side gives you the green silhouette of the hills — KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha is Origin's high-rise condominium set on a hill along Sukhumvit Road in Surasak, Si Racha, right on the hillside edge of the town centre · The tower stands 36 storeys and was completed in 2017, and some units are rented nightly through Trip.com and Agoda, so you can stay even if you don't own a unit · What people talk about most is the rooftop infinity sky pool with 360-degree bay views, the onsen, tatami room, golf simulator, fitness centre, and studio to 1-bedroom units of 24–35 sqm with a washer and kitchenette · From around THB 900–1,400/night, scored around 7.6 from real reviews

body.html: An overview of who KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha suits — if we put it as simply as possible, this isn't a "hotel" in the usual sense, but a high-rise condominium by Origin where some units are rented out nightly by owners and unit managers through platforms like Trip.com and Agoda. So what you get is the feel of staying in a "luxury condo by the sea" more than having a full hotel front desk · It works really well for people coming to work in the Eastern Seaboard industrial zone — engineers, factory managers, logistics and port staff — who want a private unit with a washer and kitchenette to actually live in for weeks or months · It suits couples who want a sea view and a photogenic pool on a modest budget, since reviews from couples rate the location fairly highly · And it suits small families or groups of friends using Si Racha as a base for day trips to Pattaya · As for anyone looking for a beachfront resort where you can walk straight down to swim in the sea, or a chain hotel with 24-hour room service and a fully staffed lobby, this place may not be the right fit, because its heart is "a condo unit for rent + premium-condo shared facilities," not hotel-style service

Location and getting around — KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha sits at 77 Moo 4, Sukhumvit Road, Surasak, Si Racha, a hillside area that climbs up from the town, so the higher units get views of both Si Racha Bay and the town below at once · From the building it's about a 5-minute drive to Robinson Si Racha, the main shopping centre with a supermarket, restaurants and a cinema · Close to Wat Khao Phutthakhodom (around 1 km), a popular city viewpoint with a large Buddha, and St Paul Convent School Si Racha · For those working here, the condo is an easy drive to the port and Laem Chabang industrial estate, roughly 15–30 minutes depending on the spot, as well as the Pinthong and Amata City industrial zones · Importantly, it's only about a 15–20 min drive from Pattaya and about an hour from Suvarnabhumi and U-Tapao airports, so you can use it as a base for both work and travel · There's a Japanese restaurant in front of the building and a convenience store in the lobby, while the wider Si Racha area is known for its seafood and a Japanese community with plenty of ramen and grill spots · The honest note is that this location "needs a car or motorbike" to be convenient, because the condo sits on a hill a fair walk from the eating and sightseeing spots, and the Sukhumvit stretch through Si Racha gets quite busy at rush hour

"Went up to the top-floor pool in the evening and it was a wow — the bay and city views are gorgeous, the pool water seems to flow right into the sea · The room was clean, having a washer in the unit is really handy, and staying here while working around Laem Chabang is far better value than a hotel. Just a five-minute drive to Robinson."

Room types and decor — because it's a condo, the units rented nightly aren't all decorated the same way; it depends on each owner, but the basic layouts are similar · The entry-level option is a studio of around 24 sqm, an open-plan room that combines the bed, a lounge corner and a kitchenette in one space, good for one person or a couple · Step up to a 1-bedroom of around 30–35 sqm that clearly separates the bedroom from the living area, suited to couples or longer stays · And there are larger 2-bedroom, duplex and penthouse units for families or anyone wanting more space · The standard in-room features many reviews mention are air conditioning, an in-unit washer, a smart TV, a rain shower, a fridge and an equipped kitchenette, so you can genuinely live as if at home · Most of the decor is a bright-toned modern style, with large glazed windows for the view and natural light · A difference worth knowing is that rooms facing the sea (sea view) and rooms facing the town (city view) feel very different — many people say a high-floor sea-view unit feels like a completely different product from a city-view one, so if you're coming for the view, choose carefully · The note is that furniture and upkeep depend on the owner; some units are brand-new and spotless, others show signs of wear, so look at real photos and reviews of that specific unit before booking

Facilities, the pool and shared areas — this is what gets KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha talked about most, because the shared facilities go all out at a level that's rare in a condo at this price · The highlight is the rooftop infinity pool (sky pool) opening onto 360-degree views of Si Racha Bay; evening to dusk is the popular time when people head up to swim, chill and photograph the sunset over the bay · The upper floors also have a sea-view fitness centre, an onsen room (Japanese-style soaking baths) and a tatami room, reflecting the large Japanese resident community in Si Racha · Downstairs and within the building there's a golf simulator, a home theatre, a co-working space, landscaped shared areas facing the sea, a convenience store in the lobby, parking and a key-card access system · Reviews agree the shared areas are beautiful and more complete than the price suggests, especially the sky pool and the fitness centre with its good views · The honest thing to know is that, because this is a condo with both real residents and nightly guests, access to some shared facilities may have rules or limited hours, and certain amenities (such as the onsen or golf simulator) may require checking with the building management or the owner about how much nightly guests can use — unlike a hotel where everything is open to guests automatically, so it's worth checking with whoever you rent from when you book

Food and places around it — to be straight, this is not a hotel with a buffet restaurant or included breakfast, because it's a condo, so eating relies mainly on the location and your in-room kitchen · The upside is there's a convenience store in the lobby for easy snacks and essentials, and a Japanese restaurant in front of the building for simple meals · Most units have a kitchenette with a fridge and utensils, so you can cook for yourself or reheat food, which suits longer stays on a budget · Importantly, Si Racha is an area where the food is good and very varied — fresh seafood, ramen and Japanese grill spots thanks to a large Japanese community, plus cafes and restaurants in Robinson just a 5-minute drive away · Many guests choose to eat out and alternate with cooking in their room, which is flexible and easy on the budget · Overall, food isn't something to expect in-building service for, but it's an advantage of the location, with plenty of spots around — as long as you have a car or are willing to call a ride to the place you want, you won't run short on choices

Service and check-in — this is the point that differs most clearly from a hotel and is worth understanding before you book · Because each unit is managed by a different owner or rental agent, the standard of welcome and check-in isn't the same across every unit · Some units have staff meet you at the lobby for check-in and take you up to the room; others use a system of sending you a lockbox code or key card to let yourself in (self check-in) · Those who were impressed say many owners reply quickly, are kind, give good tips on restaurants and getting around, and that the room matched the photos · But to be fair, some people note that the pre-stay coordination requires you to sort out all the details yourself — the key-handover time, parking, and using the shared areas — which can get messy if the owner is slow to reply · The picture you get is that "convenience depends on the owner you book with" more than a uniform hotel standard · The advice is, before booking, to message the owner clearly about the check-in process, key collection and return times, parking, and rights to use the pool/onsen/fitness centre, to avoid misunderstandings on the day

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — gathered from Trip.com, Agoda and condo information on property websites, and the picture is fairly mixed in an understandable way · On the praise side: the rooftop infinity sky pool with 360-degree bay views is beautiful and a real selling point; the shared areas are more complete than the price suggests, including fitness, onsen, tatami and co-working; high-floor sea-view units are good value with a nice atmosphere; units have a washer and kitchenette suited to longer stays; the location is central, near Robinson and Laem Chabang; and some owners look after guests impressively well · Couples in particular rate the location fairly highly · On the note side: the thing mentioned most is the inconsistency from being a condo with many owners, where room standards and the welcome vary by unit; city-view rooms feel much more ordinary than sea-view ones; you need a car to be convenient because it's on a hill away from eating and sightseeing spots; nightly guests' access to some shared facilities needs checking first; and there's no full hotel-style service · The overall score of around 7.6 reflects that the building and shared areas are good, but the experience depends on choosing the unit and the owner · Most of these gripes can be managed by picking a well-reviewed unit, choosing a high-floor sea-view room, and talking to the owner clearly before you travel, rather than being a problem with the building itself

"The shared areas are seriously good for a condo at this price — there's an onsen and a sky pool with sea views · But you have to know it's a condo, not a hotel; you sort out check-in with the owner yourself. The room I booked turned out to be city view, so it wasn't as wow as I expected. Next time I'll pick a high-floor sea-view unit and ask about parking clearly first."

Price comparison and value — because it's rented by many different owners, the nightly rate shifts by unit, season and view · Generally a studio to 1-bedroom starts from around THB 900–1,400/night at normal rates, while high-floor sea-view units, larger rooms, or peak season go higher · Compared with monthly rentals at around THB 9,000–14,000/month for a 1-bedroom (and a sea-view studio around THB 7,000–10,000/month), you'll see that for longer stays negotiating a monthly rate with the owner is far better value than booking nightly · Compared with other hotels in Si Racha and Laem Chabang, KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha feels good value in the sense of "a luxury-condo feel + premium shared facilities" at an ordinary rental price, especially if you get a high-floor sea-view unit and get to use the sky pool and onsen · The trade-off is no hotel-style service, no breakfast, and consistency depending on the owner · If you're planning to use Si Racha as a base for work in the industrial zone or for day trips to Pattaya, and you don't mind looking after yourself condo-style, then this price for the view and facilities you get is very good value

What to know before booking — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · One, understand first that this is a condo for nightly rental, not a hotel, so there's no 24-hour reception or room service · Two, if the view matters to you, request a high-floor Sea View unit right when you book, because city-view and sea-view rooms differ markedly · Three, look at real photos and reviews of the unit you'll book, since each is a different owner with different standards · Four, message the owner clearly about check-in, key collection and return times, parking, and rights to use the pool/onsen/fitness centre, because some facilities may have conditions for nightly guests · Five, arrange a car or a travel plan, because the condo is on a hill away from eating and sightseeing spots; if you don't have a car, check local ride services · Six, sea-view units fill up fast over long weekends, so book ahead, compare several platforms, and choose free cancellation first if your plans aren't firm

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha is the stay that suits best for anyone wanting a luxury sea-side condo feel with a sky pool and onsen, at an affordable rental price, on the hillside in central Si Racha — whether you're coming to work in the Eastern Seaboard industrial zone, staying for weeks or months, or using it as a base for day trips to Pattaya · The rooftop infinity pool with 360-degree bay views, the sea-view fitness centre, the Japanese-style onsen and tatami, units with a washer and kitchenette, plus a location near Robinson, Laem Chabang and Pattaya, make it good value in the sense of "shared facilities for the price" — to the point that finding a rival in the area isn't easy · But because it's a condo with many owners rather than a hotel, what you have to allow for is the inconsistency of the room and the welcome depending on the unit, no full hotel service, and needing a car to be convenient · If you can accept these conditions and choose a well-reviewed high-floor sea-view unit — KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha really can deliver "a view and lifestyle beyond its price," and that's why it scores around 7.6 from real reviews

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha

faq.q: Is KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha a hotel or a condo?
faq.a: It's a high-rise condominium by Origin Property, completed in 2017, 36 storeys with 722 units · some units are rented out nightly by owners and unit managers through platforms like Trip.com and Agoda, so you can stay even if you don't own one · but there's no full hotel-style service, and check-in and room standards depend on each unit's owner

faq.q: Where is KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha · where can you get to?
faq.a: It's at 77 Moo 4, Sukhumvit Road, Surasak, Si Racha, Chonburi, on the hillside in central Si Racha · about a 5-minute drive to Robinson Si Racha, near Wat Khao Phutthakhodom (~1 km) and St Paul Convent School · close to the Laem Chabang estate and port (~15–30 min), about 15–20 minutes from Pattaya, and about an hour from Suvarnabhumi and U-Tapao airports · this location is most convenient if you have a car

faq.q: What's the starting price at KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha · what room types are there?
faq.a: Nightly rates start from around THB 900–1,400/night for a studio to 1-bedroom, depending on the unit, view and season · there are studios ~24 sqm, 1-bedroom 30–35 sqm, up to 2-bedroom, duplex and penthouse units · units usually have a washer and kitchenette · for longer stays, try negotiating a monthly rate (around THB 7,000–14,000/month), which is far better value

faq.q: What pool and facilities does KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha have?
faq.a: The highlight is the rooftop infinity pool (sky pool) with 360-degree views of Si Racha Bay · there's a sea-view fitness centre, an onsen room, a tatami room, a golf simulator, a home theatre, a co-working space, a convenience store in the lobby, a Japanese restaurant in front of the building, parking and a key-card system · nightly guests' access to some shared facilities should be checked with the owner or building management first

faq.q: Who is KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people coming to work in the Eastern Seaboard industrial zone (Laem Chabang/EEC), couples wanting a sea view and a nice pool, and long-stay guests of weeks to months, since units have a washer and kitchenette · it's also convenient as a base for day trips to Pattaya if you have a car · if you're looking for a beachfront resort or a hotel with full 24-hour service, a chain hotel in Si Racha, Bang Saen or Pattaya may suit you better

faq.q: How should you prepare before booking KnightsBridge The Ocean Sriracha?
faq.a: Because it's a condo with many owners, we recommend looking at real photos and reviews of the unit you'll book, requesting a high-floor Sea View room if you're coming for the view, and messaging the owner clearly about the check-in process, key collection and return times, parking, and rights to use the pool/onsen/fitness centre · also arrange a car or a ride plan, since the condo is on a hill away from eating and sightseeing spots · over long weekends sea-view units fill up fast, so book ahead and choose free cancellation first
